title: Ninth commandment (CCC 2517–2533)
hookLine: purity of heart lets us see God in others

cards: A smudge on a pair of glasses. The wearer doesn't notice it at first. The world just seems a little gray, a little blurred at the edges, and faces look tired.
Then the glasses come off, get a wipe on a shirt, go back on, and everything is sharp again. Nothing out there changed. The lens did.
The ninth commandment, in the Catechism, turns out to be about lenses: what we look at people through.

teach.h: BLESSED ARE THE CLEAN OF HEART.
teach.b: As the Catechism counts them, the ninth commandment forbids coveting a neighbor's wife: disordered desire, which it calls concupiscence.
But it builds the whole section on a line from the Sermon on the Mount, in the Douay-Rheims: "Blessed are the clean of heart: for they shall see God." The heart here isn't just feelings.

teach.h: THE HEART: WHERE INTENTIONS ARE BORN.
teach.b: The Catechism calls it the seat of the moral personality; in plain words, where intentions are born. The pure of heart have tuned mind and will to God's ways, in charity, chastity, love of truth and faith.
Then the promise opens in a surprising direction.

Seeing God is the end of the road, but purity of heart lets us see according to God now: the other person as a neighbor, and the human body, ours and others', as a temple of the Holy Spirit. That's the smudge wiped off.

teach.h: SEE OTHERS AS GOD SEES THEM.
teach.b: Not a refusal to look at people, but a way of looking that doesn't reduce them. How does a heart get clean?
The Catechism names a struggle and its helps: chastity, purity of intention, purity of vision, discipline over what feelings and imagination dwell on, and prayer.
It adds modesty, which protects the private center of a person and refuses to unveil what should stay hidden. And it's grace as well as effort: no one cleans the lens entirely alone.
The ninth commandment is less a list of things not to see than a promise about what you'll be able to see.

how: Catholics pray for purity of heart and examine their thoughts and looks before confession; the Church teaches chastity, modesty, purity of intention and prayer as helps in this struggle.

o: thinking only of heaven, never of people
never having a single unwanted thought
a heart tuned to God that sees others clearly

games.q: they shall see god — tap the pairs.
p: a temple of the Holy Spirit
guards the private center of a person

s: in this teaching, the heart means only feelings
the Catechism calls it the seat of the moral personality, where intentions are born.
the Catechism says purity of heart helps us see others now, not only God later
it lets us receive the other as a neighbor, and see the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit.
the Catechism says a pure heart comes from willpower alone
it names prayer and grace alongside effort.

games.q: the beatitude promises the clean of heart that they shall see God. when does the Catechism say that seeing begins?
o: already now, in how we see others.
games.why: seeing God is the goal, but the Catechism says purity of heart already lets us see according to God: the other as a neighbor, the body as a temple.

practice: Bring to mind three faces: someone you love, someone you pass every day without really seeing, and someone you find hard. One at a time, set down the label you usually put on them and look for the person underneath.
If you pray, ask to see each one as God sees them; if not, simply let them be more than you thought.

wordCard.voice: Purity of heart. A heart tuned to God in love, chastity, truth and faith, which, in Catholic teaching, begins to see others, and God, clearly. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: the clean, or pure, of heart — Matthew 5:8.

carryVoice: Your line: they shall see god. A clean heart changes what the eyes can see. Until tomorrow.
